title: Do three ways of adding three terms agree?
description: Negative seven plus ten plus negative eleven is added in three different ways and the answers are compared. Keeko doubts the ways and thinks only one of them can be right.
teaching_notes: One idea: when three terms are added, the pair we add first does not change the sum. Watch for children who think different ways must give different answers.

source: Add (−7) + 10 + (−11) in three different ways and compare.
video_script.why: The child sees that the pair added first in a sum of three terms does not change the answer.
video_script.substitution: Add the first two terms, then the last two, then the two negative terms, and compare the three answers.
video_script.anchor: Three terms to add: negative seven, ten and negative eleven
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks that three different ways of adding must give three different answers, so only one of them can be right.
video_script.payoff_line: All three ways give negative eight

final_answer.spoken: negative seven plus ten plus negative eleven is negative eight in every way of adding

never_show: a different total for any of the three ways
video_script.design: One idea: the pair added first does not change the sum of three terms. Assumes adding two integers. Wrong idea: different ways give different answers, so only one is right. The three terms stay on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; three terms (−7) + 10 + (−11) with three curved arrows showing three different ways to pair them

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.terms: the three terms appear in a row
marks.ask: three curved arrows appear over different pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='terms'/>Look at negative seven plus ten plus negative eleven.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We can add these three terms in three different ways. Do the answers agree?

beats.on_screen: the three terms stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: three terms 2, 3, 4 with a curved line around the first two, then a second line around the sum and the last term

marks.pair: a curved line closes around two terms
marks.next: the third term is added to the result

narration: <bookmark mark='pair'/>To add three terms, we add two of them first.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Then we add the third term to that result. We are free to choose which two to add first.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three terms, negative seven, ten and negative eleven.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum in three different ways, and a comparison

marks.find: the words three different ways and compare are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to add them in three different ways, and then compare the answers.

marks.first: the first two terms are paired and worked out as 3

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, add the first two terms first, so negative seven plus ten is three.
<bookmark mark='then'/>Then three plus negative eleven gives negative eight.

marks.last: the last two terms are paired and worked out as −1

narration: <bookmark mark='last'/>Step two, add the last two terms first, so ten plus negative eleven is negative one.
<bookmark mark='then'/>Then negative seven plus negative one is again negative eight.

marks.neg: the two negative terms are paired and worked out as −18

narration: <bookmark mark='neg'/>Step three, add the two negative terms first, so negative seven plus negative eleven is negative eighteen.
<bookmark mark='then'/>Then negative eighteen plus ten is again negative eight.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (−7) + 10 + (−11) = −8 in any order or grouping

marks.ans: the three results are placed side by side and the answer is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>All three ways give negative eight, so the pair we add first does not change the sum.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows: three ways, three answers, only one is right; beside it the three results side by side, all the same; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the three equal results glow and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks three different ways must give different answers, so only one is right.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But every way uses the same three terms, and the pair we add first does not matter.
